solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Bosnian-Serb hitman ably adapted to take over role opposite 8

parts.note: Gavrilo Princip, the Bosnian Serb who shot Archduke Franz Ferdinand in 1914

indicators.note: the rearranged letters take in, or hold, the cricket abbreviation for an over
something adapted has been altered, so the letters of the word ably are rearranged

parts.note: O is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A notorious assassin's skills are reworked so he can be cast in a stage part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adapted' turns ABLY into ALBY, and 'to take' puts O inside it to make ALBOY. In British pantomime the principal boy, the young male hero, is traditionally played by a woman, opposite the dame (8 down).
explanation.definitionFit: In British pantomime the young hero is the lead role played against the comic drag character of 8 down.

clue.text: Steak, for the most part, way over cooked

indicators.note: in a down clue the way sits over, that is around, the other piece

parts.note: a road is a way

indicators.note: only the majority of the word steak is used, its final letters being dropped

explanation.surface: Someone complains their steak has mostly been cooked far too long.
explanation.walkthrough: 'way over cooked' reads like overcooked, but 'over' is the containment signal: in a down clue the road sits over, around, most of the steak.
explanation.definitionFit: Meat cooked in an oven or over a fire has been roasted, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Bushranger reporting rogue elephant running round Eastern Denmark

indicators.note: the elephant's name is put around the other letters

parts.note: Nelly (Nellie) is the stock name for an elephant, as in the song Nellie the Elephant who ran away
DK is the international vehicle code for Denmark

explanation.surface: A news report about an Australian outlaw and a runaway elephant loose in eastern Denmark.
explanation.walkthrough: Ned Kelly was the most famous Australian bushranger, an armour-wearing outlaw of the 1870s; 'reporting' simply links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Bushrangers were Australian bandits of the colonial era, and this outlaw is the best known of them.

clue.text: Holy Island regularly ignored His own law

indicators.note: every other letter of His own law is skipped, keeping the alternate ones

explanation.surface: A holy island where people routinely disregard what God decreed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly ignored' drops the first, third and so on of HIS OWN LAW, leaving the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters.
explanation.definitionFit: This small Hebridean island is a centre of early Christianity, founded as a monastery by St Columba.

clue.text: Prepared tea tray he'd ordered

indicators.note: the letters of tea tray he'd are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A tea tray he had asked for is ready and waiting.
explanation.definitionFit: Being poised and ready for immediate use is exactly what this idiom means.

clue.text: Created German tabloid podcast

indicators.note: a podcast is heard rather than read, so the newspaper's name is taken as spoken

parts.note: Bild is Germany's best-selling tabloid newspaper

explanation.surface: A German tabloid newspaper launches a podcast.
explanation.definitionFit: Something constructed or made has been created, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Artist loved by 16, unknown, niche, upwardly mobile, bespectacled

parts.note: Y is one of the algebraic letters standing for an unknown quantity
a niche is a nook; upwardly mobile in a down clue writes it bottom to top, and bespectacled puts it between two round lenses, drawn as a pair of rings, O and O

explanation.surface: An artist adored by a famous man is described as ambitious and wearing glasses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bespectacled' does double duty: the glasses drawn as two rings both supply letters and enclose the reversed niche, so the parse shows this stretch as one piece. 16 is JOHN of 16/22, so 'loved by 16' points to John Lennon.
explanation.definitionFit: The Japanese conceptual artist married John Lennon, whose first name is the 16 across entry.

clue.text: Visiting Japan, Tom? I'm Ed, a method actor specialising in drag …

indicators.note: the answer pays a visit inside the run of words Japan, Tom? I'm Ed, a method

parts.words: Japan, Tom? I'm Ed, a method

explanation.surface: A method actor named Ed introduces himself to Tom while touring Japan, explaining he plays women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Visiting' signals the letters sitting inside japAN TOM I'M ED A MEthod. The pantomime dame is a comic older woman in British Christmas pantomime, always played by a man.
explanation.definitionFit: The dame role is a traditional cross-dressing comic part, so its player is a performer who works in drag.

clue.text: … playing in drag titles; a major star

indicators.note: the letters are playing about, put in a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Continuing from 8 down: the drag actor plays title roles, being a big name.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins this to 8 down so the surface reads on, but the clue stands alone: 'playing' rearranges IN DRAG TITLES A.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer at the top of the bill is a major star, an idiomatic equivalent.

clue.text: Male baddie, one getting stripped for some fun with The Widow Twankey?

definitions.text: some fun with The Widow Twankey?

indicators.note: each of the three words loses its outer letters, leaving its insides

explanation.surface: A male villain gets undressed for a bit of fun with a pantomime widow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting stripped' peels the ends off MALE, BADDIE and ONE. Widow Twankey is the comic dame in the pantomime about the boy with the lamp.
explanation.definitionFit: Widow Twankey is the hero's mother in this pantomime, so a jolly show featuring her is that panto.

clue.text: Run with a dribble to bamboozle the French

parts.note: to bamboozle someone is to trick them
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A footballer runs with the ball at his feet to fool the French defence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run with a dribble' sounds like football, but here it is a liquid flowing in a thin stream.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin, slow flow of liquid is a liquid running in a dribble, so the verb fits as a paraphrase.

clue.text: Name model sporting hat

indicators.note: the model is sporting, or wearing, the hat around it

parts.note: tile is old slang for a hat
the Model T was Ford's famous car, so model gives T

explanation.surface: A fashion model is wearing a hat on the catwalk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sporting' has the hat TILE go round T, the Model T Ford: TI-T-LE.
explanation.definitionFit: What something is called is its title, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: English golfer with established club

parts.note: a wood is a type of golf club

explanation.surface: A golfer from England with a club that has been around for years.
explanation.definitionFit: Lee Westwood is a leading English professional who was ranked world number one.

clue.text: New Amazon rival knocking out five for a tenner as advertised on the radio

definitions.text: a tenner as advertised on the radio
definitions.note: a tenner said aloud sounds like a tenor, a high male singing voice

indicators.note: the letters are made new, put into a different order
the Roman numeral for five is knocked out of the words before they are rearranged

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: A new online retailer rivalling Amazon offers money off: five removed for every ten pounds, as heard in a radio ad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocking out' removes V from AMAZON RIVAL and 'New' rearranges what is left. The definition is itself spoken: 'tenner' heard on the radio is tenor.
explanation.definitionFit: Mario Lanza was an American operatic tenor and film star of the 1950s.

clue.text: 60ish, I'm about to see United relegated from league in 3D

indicators.note: turning about reverses the letters of I'm
the shortened league sits in among the three Ds

parts.note: read literally, 3D is three Ds

indicators.note: the abbreviation for United is sent down out of the word league

parts.note: U is the usual abbreviation for United in team names

explanation.surface: A sixty-year-old football fan is about to watch his team go down, in a three-dimensional film.
explanation.walkthrough: '3D' is read literally as three Ds, and the trimmed league goes in among them after the second; 'relegated' is football's going down, here dropping United's U.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone around sixty is in the stretch of life between youth and old age.

clue.text: Animal-loving doctor, victim of murder in US, endlessly left 12 upset

indicators.note: the last letter is cut from the placeholder name

parts.note: John Doe is the name US police give an unidentified male body

indicators.note: the letters of 12 across are upset, knocked into a new order

parts.note: the answer to 12 across, which means name

explanation.surface: An animal-loving doctor, an American murder victim, left a name tangled up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts JOHN DOE to JOHN DO, and 'upset' turns TITLE (12 across) into ITTLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Hugh Lofting's fictional physician could talk to animals and gave up humans to treat them.

clue.text: Builders tea accompaniments? About right

indicators.note: the biscuits go about, or around, the abbreviation for right

parts.note: bickies is informal British for biscuits, eaten with tea

explanation.surface: Builders' tea comes with biscuits, more or less correctly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Builders tea' suggests the strong British brew, but 'Builders' alone is the definition. 'About' puts R inside BICKIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Brickie is British informal for a bricklayer, a kind of builder.

clue.text: Shift miles left — not right!

indicators.note: not right means without the abbreviation for right

parts.note: food left is food over, as in left over

explanation.surface: A driver is told to move miles to the left, not the right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' is not a direction but 'remaining', i.e. OVER; 'not' removes R from it to give OVE.
explanation.definitionFit: To shift something is to change its position, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Birmingham team at home one behind, getting the crowd screaming?

definitions.text: one behind, getting the crowd screaming?

parts.note: Aston Villa is a Birmingham football club
in means at home

explanation.surface: A Birmingham football side, a goal down in a home match, has its supporters yelling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one behind' looks like a losing scoreline; it is the pantomime baddie lurking behind the hero while the audience screams "He's behind you!"
explanation.definitionFit: In pantomime the audience shouts warnings at the baddie creeping up behind the hero.

clue.text: Scrumpy flagon finally gulped, Ms Fitzgerald's due off stage by midnight

indicators.note: the cider gulps down, taking inside, the last letter

parts.note: scrumpy is rough farmhouse cider from the west of England

indicators.note: only the end letter of flagon is taken

parts.note: Ella Fitzgerald, the American jazz singer

explanation.surface: A singer knocks back rough cider from a flagon and must leave the stage before midnight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' picks N, which CIDER has 'gulped': CI-N-DER. The 's is 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The fairytale heroine must leave the ball before the clock strikes twelve, when the spell breaks.

clue.text: Business graduate stuck in Galician city — what a pain!

indicators.note: the business qualification is stuck inside the city name

parts.note: Lugo is a city in Galicia, north-west Spain
an MBA is a Master of Business Administration

explanation.surface: An MBA holder stuck in a Spanish city exclaims at how tedious it is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'what a pain!' sounds like exasperation at the city, but it frames the definition: an ache.
explanation.definitionFit: Lower back ache is a specific, familiar kind of pain.

clue.text: See 16
Fiddle, without piano, becoming more mellow

indicators.note: the musical abbreviation for piano is left out

parts.note: to tamper is to fiddle with something
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly

explanation.surface: A violin played with no piano accompaniment sounds gentler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fiddle' looks like a violin but is the verb, meddle.
explanation.definitionFit: Tamer means gentler, less wild, a comparative synonym for more mellow.

clue.text: Yours truly in bed. A heavenly sight

indicators.note: the speaker is placed in the bed

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
yours truly is a jokey way of saying me

explanation.surface: Someone lying in bed declares themselves a glorious sight.
explanation.definitionFit: A bright object with a glowing tail seen in the night sky is a heavenly body.

clue.text: Lighter, small Jersey perhaps

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
a Jersey is a breed of dairy cattle

explanation.surface: A cigarette lighter and a small jersey, as if from a lost-property box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lighter' is not a cigarette lighter but a flat barge for unloading ships; 'Jersey' is a cow, not a sweater.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat-bottomed boat for carrying goods to and from ships is a lighter.

clue.text: Source of ready cash guarded by stingy butcher

indicators.note: the cash machine is guarded, held inside, by the word for stingy

parts.note: mean means stingy
an ATM is a cash machine

explanation.surface: A miserly butcher keeps a close watch on a cash machine.
explanation.definitionFit: A butcher deals in meat, so a meat-seller is an apt informal name.

clue.text: Armour plate, 50% iron lining, copper bottom

indicators.note: half the iron lines, or sits alongside, the copper

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: half of the word iron, its first two letters, is taken

parts.note: ass is slang for bottom

explanation.surface: Description of a suit of armour plated with iron and with a copper-bottomed base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper bottom' looks like one phrase (copper-bottomed) but splits: copper is a chemical symbol and bottom is a separate synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: A cuirass is a breastplate and backplate worn together as body armour.

clue.text: Angry Nimrod moans about wife seeing a funny little bloke in a flat cap

definitions.text: a funny little bloke in a flat cap

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go about the abbreviation for wife
the letters of Nimrod moans are stirred up into a new order

explanation.surface: Nimrod complains furiously about his wife's reaction to a comic little man in a cap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Angry' rearranges NIMROD MOANS, placed 'about' W. Norman Wisdom was a British comedian famous for his slapstick character in a too-small suit and flat cap.
explanation.definitionFit: This short slapstick comedian wore a skewed cloth cap as his trademark costume.
